title: The tools shall be able to process a set of multiple WARC files at the same time. For this purpose, the tools will allow you to choose/group them by: explicit naming, wildcard name matching, size limitation, number of items
The tools shall be able to scale to process large collections using distributed processing and data transport
The tools shall offer best possible performance to correctly process large collections (I/O bound)
The tools shall be able to run on multiple machines but will not provide functionality for dealing with hardware failures (out of scope)
Implementation of the tools shall avoid unnecessary technology dependencies and shall not include development of partner-specific integration technologies
The tools shall be compliant with Java development environments, by using web services,  RESTful APIs, etc
The tools shall provide logging facilities, for example, to follow command progression, i.e. process duration, output levels, etc
The tools shall provide enhanced usability by providing easy to adapt shell script wrappers for the major commands
It shall be possible to operate the tools in modes that restrict their effects to selected collection subsets. For example, select by name
The workflow system shall have a configurable management strategy for migration from ARCs to WARCs.
The migration workflow system will be driven by command line tools and scripts
Migration configurations can be built with a Web User Interface
Active migrations can be monitored, paused, and restarted (a console application) with a Web User Interface

Pre and post conversion actions will be provided for at each level of the migration, e.g. record,
 WARC, job
The migration workflow shall provide a clear Application Programming Interface (API) to handle the migration process and default configuration
The migration API will require inclusion of only one header file.
A configuration must be provided explicitly, errors should be generated in the absence of a configuration
The user shall be able to provide metadata related to the conversion that will be stored in the converted files (e.g., institution, context, crawler, collection name, ...)
automatically generated migration metadata be stored
content: It shall be possible to request that automatically generated migration metadata be stored in the converted files (e.g., OS/Kernel type, original ARC name, ARC size, ARC digests, conversion timestamp, ARC record offset, ...)

title: IIPC members should provide us with the default METADATA they want to be included for migration.
The migration workflow shall be able to call external tools and services (e.g., database queries, shell commands, web service).

The migration process shall use persistent, opaque, unique, and global identifiers for records
 access.
A (default) external tool (e.g., ClamAV) will be used to scan files before conversion (pre-conversion step).
The API should be flexible enough to allow external tools such as JHOVE, DROID to be used for file format identification.

The ARC to WARC migration should be able to run on multiple machines that will be easy to
 deploy. This may be achieved by using a simple messaging infrastructure
Logging during the migration may be turned on/off at any time.
Deduplication may be run before migration, inside a batch process.
Duplicate detection shall find and report WARC records with the same checksums. A centralised database will be used to store previously processed records, against which new ones will be compared.
To validate that the migration succeeded, arc_warc_verify will use the METADATA included in the newly generated WARC files to match records with their corresponding ARC files (see FR4, and FR5).
Core validation shall use payload checksum comparisons
Sampling will be provided where applicable to quickly validate the conversions (FR 15.1 and FR 18 for example).
Validation shall use Heritrixs arcreader to double check that the original ARC record was correctly converted to WARC.
It shall be possible to perform a round trip validation: migrate the newly created WARC file back to ARC and compare both checksums (NFR 5)
It shall be possible to repackage WARC files by filtering records based on URL (regular expressions)
It shall be possible to repackage WARC files by filtering records based on MIME-Types.
It shall be possible to repackage WARC files by filtering records based on size.
It shall be possible to repackage WARC files by filtering records based on timestamp (e.g., dates interval).
It shall be possible to repackage WARC files by filtering on any field in the WARC specification.
Repackaging will allow pre and post record, file and job operations
Pre operation can prevent a file or record being processed by returning value
Each repackaged WARC file shall include a user-defined METADATA record which will describe the extraction context (e.g., filter used, involved WARC files, ... - see also FR4).
The migration framework shall provide tools to build reports from WARC files
Repackaging filters can be used by the summary module
It shall be possible to export summaries in various formats (e.g., XML, CSV)
Enhance the WARC browser to display aggregated WARCs summaries in its UI
Enhance the WARC browser to display a manifest of WARC files and their locations
Provide a "diff" tool to compare WARC sets based on defined criteria (e.g., timestamp, hostname, etc.)
Provide a way to view crawls deltas for quality assurance
Implement WARC browser server side rewriting
Integrate a proxy mode inside the WARC browser
Integrate the full-text search (search-tools project) module with the WARC browser to provide users with WARC indexing/searching capabilities.

Software checkpoints (such as start-trans, end-trans) may be added during processing for managing atomic transactions (e.g., operations on a file), except where operating system limitations would prohibit it.
